notes:
Account: Pyrite Capital Systems (global payments platform) — very procurement-heavy, security-first.

Summary of ask:
- Dedicated GPU pools for inference with reserved baseline capacity + burst pool.
- Throughput guarantees and a clear credit schedule for any SLA misses.
- Tight latency SLOs on core payment assistant and reranker (P95/P99 targets).
- Maintenance windows must be agreed and should avoid US market peak hours (13:00-18:00 ET).
- KMS/HSM support + audit logs + data residency in US and EU.

Recent call notes (shorthand):
- 2026-02-03 discovery + infra deep-dive (ff recording ff-20260203-8f4a32). AE Maya + SE Ravi + Pyrite infra lead (Connor V.) present.
- Pyrite: "We cannot accept >1 minute planned downtime during market hours" — pushing for narrower maintenance windows.
- SE requested sample kernel/quantization plan for p95 latency improvements; Pyrite will provide traffic profile by 2/10.
- Pricing sensitivity: prefers committed monthly billing, asks for uplift for 99.995% vs 99.99%.

Technical requirements (from calls/email):
- Workloads: real-time payment chat (avg request payload ~600 tokens), policy/compliance QA (batch embeddings), fraud reranking (short context).
- Expected steady throughput: 2k req/s across US/EU regions, peak burst 5k req/s for 30-60 minutes (cron spikes).
- Latency targets: P95 <= 120ms (chat short-turn), P99 <= 350ms; reranker P95 <= 90ms.
- Throughput guarantee: sustained baseline capacity to cover 2k req/s with autoscale thresholds; reserved GPUs planned to achieve predictable tail latency.
- KV/prefix caching required for payments-chat to reduce token compute and hit SLOs.

SLA specifics under negotiation (items to surface in draft):
- Uptime target: Pyrite requests 99.995% for critical routes; Redwood proposing 99.99% for dedicated baseline, with mitigation options (multi-region failover + fallback model) to improve effective availability.
- Credit schedule: tiered credits for monthly uptime below thresholds (example: 99.99-99.95 => 10% credit; 99.95-99.9 => 25%; <99.9 => 50%). Pyrite pushing for higher credits and pro-rated compute credits for missed throughput guarantees.
- Maintenance windows: propose 2x/week 02:00-04:00 PT for non-disruptive updates; Pyrite requests maintenance outside US market hours and advance 21-day notice for any rolling restarts affecting P95.
- Support: 1-hour P1 response, 4-hour initial remediation plan, dedicated escalation path to on-call infra lead during market hours. Pyrite demands SOC/contractual incident timelines.
- Throughput credits: explicit formula linking reserved GPU capacity to guaranteed throughput and token budgets; need a worked example for 1-month billing cycle.

Commercial/ops notes:
- Pyrite favors committed 12-month reserved capacity with monthly true-ups. Wants option to add burst credits for major events (billing at committed rate + burst uplift).
- Legal: requires PoLP (principle of least privilege) attestation and right-to-audit clause limited in scope.
- Finance: asks for an enterprise discount schedule if ARR > $500k; procurement is pushing to finalize pricing tiers before Q3 budgeting.

Open questions / follow-ups:
- SE to provide capacity plan mapping: model variant -> GPUs required -> expected P95/P99 with/without caching by 2026-02-12.
- Security to deliver KMS/HSM diagram + SOC2 attestation copy.
- AE to present SLA draft v2 with explicit credit schedule and maintenance window options by 2026-02-18.

Quotable from Pyrite CTO on call: "We need predictable latency during settlement windows — uncertainty equals lost revenue."

CRM shorthand next steps:
- Prep SLA v2 (legal + pricing) -> send 2/18.
- Joint runbook workshop (Redwood SE + Pyrite ops) week of 2/22 to validate failover, cache warmup, and burst behavior.
- Legal review kickoff 2/24.
